sections.h2: Where does a deed get recorded in Oakland County?
sections.html:
Deeds for Oakland County land are recorded by the county's Clerk/Register of Deeds. The Register of Deeds side takes the line 248-858-0597 and the email deeds@oaklandcountymi.gov, and the counter is staffed Monday through Friday from 8:30 to 4:30. The combined office is among the largest in Michigan, with almost 100 employees serving about 1.2 million residents.

Oakland County was founded in 1820, and the office still holds records from that era. The Clerk and Register of Deeds offices were merged in 1958, and only a few Michigan counties run them as one. Today the office records more than 140,000 real estate documents each year.

The county has 530,460 households and 569,537 housing units, and the Census Bureau found that 89.1% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Median selected monthly owner costs run $1,998 with a mortgage and $778 without one, which gives a sense of the mortgages and discharges that flow through the recording counter alongside deeds.

The register's public record covers deeds, mortgages, foreclosure records and personal property filings. Copies of recorded documents are available through the Oakland County Super Index back to January 1, 1964, apart from subdivision plat maps. Since November 3, 2025, UCC filings are no longer recorded separately from land records, and the land record fees apply to them.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges for an Oakland County deed?
sections.html:
One deed carries a $30 charge no matter how many pages it runs. That figure includes the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee, and Michigan's fee statute, MCL 600.2567, sets the same $30 base amount.

Oakland County Register of Deeds fees and transfer tax rates
ItemCharge
Recording a deed, mortgage or lis pendens$30.00
Each extra liber and page on a discharge or assignment$3.00
Copies$1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$5.00 per document
Treasurer's tax certificate for warranty deeds$5.00
County transfer tax$0.55 per $500 of consideration
State transfer tax$3.75 per $500 of consideration

Warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed with a covenant of warranty must be tax certified at the county treasurer's office first. If you mail a document in, the register will obtain the certificate and attach revenue stamps for you, and the $5 certificate fee goes into your payment.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies on an Oakland County sale?
sections.html:
Michigan charges transfer tax on any instrument that moves real property worth $100 or more. In Oakland County the county rate is $1.10 per $1,000 and the state rate is $7.50 per $1,000, computed on the full consideration. Exemptions exist, and the reason must appear on the face of the document.

As a worked case, a home sold at the county's $343,600 median owner-occupied value would carry about $378 in county tax and $2,577 in state tax, which is roughly $2,955 together. Michigan's two transfer tax acts, as summarized by the Oceana County register, place the tax on the seller or grantor, so budget for it on the seller's side of the closing statement.

  • Show the total value of the real property on the deed, or attach an affidavit stating it.
  • Print any exemption claimed on the document itself.
  • Ask the title company how the stamps will be purchased and paid at closing.

sections.h2: What must a document include to be recorded in Oakland County?
sections.html:
A document is accepted when it meets the format and signature rules the register lists under Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201. The office examines each one and records only those that meet statutory requirements. The legal description is also reviewed by a validation unit before the cashier handles the document.

  • Signatures must be original, with names typed or printed beneath them.
  • Names in the notary acknowledgment must match the signatures.
  • The grantee's name and address must appear on any instrument that conveys or encumbers real estate.
  • A document signed in Michigan needs a notary acknowledgment with signature, county of commission and expiration date.
  • Print in black ink, at least 10-point type, on white 20-pound paper between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • Leave a 2.5 inch blank margin at the top of the first page and 0.5 inch on all other sides.
  • State the nature of the recordable event on the first line of the first page.
  • Put the total value of the property on the document or an attached affidavit.

Documents that say a survivor takes title need a certified copy of a death certificate, or proof of death, recorded with them. Court orders must be certified and sealed by the court clerk. Older documents follow earlier rules: marital status of male grantors was required before April 6, 2017, and two witnesses were required before March 2002.

sections.h2: Can Oakland County documents be recorded electronically?
sections.html:
Yes, the register accepts e-recording through registered providers, including Corporation Service Company, eRecording Partners Network, Simplifile and HopDox. UCC documents and mortgage foreclosure documents cannot be e-recorded.

The county also runs MiPropDocs for documents that do not transfer ownership. It accepts affidavits, association liens and discharges, claims of lien, certificates of trust, discharges, lis pendens, mortgages, notices of commencement, releases and satisfactions of mortgage. A deed cannot go through it, so an owner transferring a house still needs a title company e-recording account or a paper filing.

sections.h2: How long does it take to get a recorded deed back?
sections.html:
Expect about two weeks for a document hand-carried to the counter and about two to four weeks for one sent by mail. A document that came through a title company usually returns about two weeks after recording. The register indexes and returns recorded originals by U.S. Mail unless a pickup was arranged.

Copy requests move faster. Walk-in customers get five pages as a courtesy, and larger orders are usually finished within 24 to 48 hours, with pickup in person or by mail. The office will also give a payoff figure for a foreclosure and handles redemptions on sheriff deeds and clerk deeds for people with an interest in the property. Money for a redemption is receipted and held by the treasurer until paperwork is complete.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Oakland County?
faqs.a: $30 per document, with no extra charge for page count. That amount already includes the $4.00 state survey and remonumentation fee. Discharges that cover several recorded instruments add $3.00 for each additional reference.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax certificate to record a warranty deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a warranty clause must be tax certified at the Oakland County Treasurer's Office, for a $5.00 fee, before the register will record them.

faqs.q: How far back do online Oakland County records go?
faqs.a: The Super Index covers recorded documents back to January 1, 1964, except subdivision plat maps. For older records, contact the Register of Deeds at 248-858-0597.

faqs.q: Does the Oakland County register still file UCC statements?
faqs.a: Not separately. Since November 3, 2025, UCC documents are handled with land records and the land record recording fees apply.

faqs.q: Who pays transfer tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The tax falls on the seller or grantor under the Michigan acts, and it is paid at the time of recording. County and state tax together come to about $8.60 per $1,000 of sale price in Oakland County.
